why: Source: sum contacted and total per employer size to compare contact shares, total contact share, no-contact pool comparison, plus one no-data check (about 6 steps); question: the same four statement checks on the same 9-row table with the true answer moved to the overall-share option (about 6 steps).
Source: pick the right pie, sum three slices, multiply by the respondent share (3 steps); question: pick the right pie among four, sum three slices, multiply by 18% (3 steps).

Source: two sum-and-ratio checks (group totals) plus two single-ratio checks (about 6 steps); question: the same two sum-and-ratio checks and two single-ratio threshold checks with the true answer on a single ratio (about 6 steps).

Source: total cost from fixed plus variable, then four cumulative-difference times total divided by group size checks (about 6 steps); question: identical structure with the same total-cost calculation and four group checks (about 6 steps).

Source: gridline reads of an unlabelled indexed line chart, one index-base logic check, two share ratios, one point-change comparison and one direction comparison (about 5 steps); question: the same four statement types on the same kind of chart (about 5 steps).

Source: spot that the pie is a share of the 45% subgroup, sum three slices and scale, scale single slices, dismiss the no-data option (about 5 steps); question: the same base trap with a 48% subgroup, a three-slice sum, single-slice scaling and a no-data option (about 5 steps).

Source: chain the subgroup share with the second pie (one multiplication), avoid the base trap, reject main-versus-only and no-spending statements (about 4 steps); question: identical structure with day trips instead of hotel stays (about 4 steps).
Source: respondents times first-pie share, then times second-pie share, avoiding the skip-the-first-pie trap (3 steps); question: the same two multiplications and the same trap (3 steps).

Source: value a 1% cut in claims and in operations, net a 1% revenue rise of the proportional claims rise, note the sub-cost is smaller, compare (about 5 steps); question: the same four valuations and comparison with the answer landing on revenue instead of the biggest cost (about 5 steps).

Source: maintenance hours difference times rate, electricity kWh difference times price, sum the annual saving, times three-year payback (4 steps); question: the same four steps with new numbers (4 steps).
